phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. ˹This is˺ a Book which We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ so that you may lead people out of darkness and into light, by the Will of their Lord, to the Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy—
phrases.explanation: The surah opens with the separated letters Alif-Lãm-Ra and describes the Quran as a Book revealed to the Prophet. Its purpose is to lead people from darkness into light by their Lord’s will, toward the path of the Almighty and Praiseworthy.

phrases.translation: Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe torment
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. The verse warns disbelievers of severe torment, contrasting their rejection with the sovereignty of the One who owns all creation. He owns all creation without exception.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ the ones who favour the life of this world over the Hereafter and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked. It is they who have gone far astray
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers prefer the life of this world to the Hereafter. The verse criticizes making immediate pleasure more important than the lasting life for which people are accountable. They hinder others from Allah’s way and try to make it appear crooked. Their conduct does more than reject guidance for themselves, because they also discourage others from following it. They have gone far astray. The conclusion describes the distance created by choosing worldly life and obstructing the path to Allah.

phrases.translation: We have not sent a messenger except in the language of his people to clarify ˹the message˺ for them. Then Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Each messenger is sent in the language of his people so he can clarify the message. The verse explains how revelation is made understandable to the community receiving it. Allah guides whom He wills and leaves whom He wills to stray. The verse places ultimate guidance with Him rather than with a messenger’s power to compel belief. Allah is Almighty and All-Wise. His power and wisdom frame the guidance and judgment described in the verse.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, ˹ordering him,˺ “Lead your people out of darkness and into light, and remind them of Allah’s days ˹of favour˺.” Surely in this are signs for whoever is steadfast, grateful
phrases.explanation: Moses is commanded to lead his people from darkness into light through Allah’s signs. The image presents revelation as a way out of ignorance and oppression. Moses is also told to remind the people of Allah’s days of favor. Remembering past deliverance can strengthen gratitude and trust during present hardship. The signs benefit those who are patient and grateful. The verse joins perseverance in difficulty with appreciation of Allah’s blessings.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ when Moses said to his people, “Remember Allah’s favour upon you when He rescued you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with dreadful torment—slaughtering your sons and keeping your women. That was a severe test from your Lord
phrases.explanation: Moses reminds the Israelites that Allah rescued them from Pharaoh’s people. The rescue is presented as a favor after a period of oppression. Pharaoh’s people killed the sons and spared the women while imposing dreadful torment. Moses recalls these acts so the people remember the severity of what they escaped. This was a severe test from their Lord. The memory of oppression and rescue calls the people to recognize both their hardship and Allah’s deliverance.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when your Lord proclaimed, ‘If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more. But if you are ungrateful, surely My punishment is severe.’”
phrases.explanation: Allah promises more favor to those who are grateful and warns of severe punishment for ingratitude. Gratitude is therefore a response to blessing that shapes what follows, not merely a feeling.

phrases.translation: Moses added, “If you along with everyone on earth were to be ungrateful, then ˹know that˺ Allah is indeed Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.”
phrases.explanation: Even if everyone on earth were ungrateful, Allah would remain Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy. Human gratitude does not add to His greatness, and human rejection cannot diminish it. His praise is independent of human acknowledgment.

phrases.translation: Have you not ˹already˺ received the stories of those who were before you: the people of Noah, ’Âd, Thamûd, and those after them? Only Allah knows how many they were. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs,
phrases.explanation: The audience is asked to remember Noah’s people, Aad, Thamud, and later communities. Their histories show that rejection of messengers has occurred across many generations. Only Allah knows the full number of those peoples, and their messengers came with clear proofs. They were given evidence before they responded to the warning.

phrases.translation: but they put their hands over their mouths and said, “We totally reject what you have been sent with, and we are certainly in alarming doubt about what you are inviting us to.”
phrases.explanation: The people cover their mouths and reject the message, saying they are in alarming doubt. Their response is a deliberate refusal even after clear proofs have been presented. They tell the messengers that they doubt the invitation. The verse records their resistance as a choice, not as evidence that no message or warning reached them.

phrases.translation: Their messengers asked ˹them˺, “Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?
phrases.explanation: The messengers ask whether anyone can doubt Allah, the Originator of the heavens and earth. The question points to creation as evidence of the One who calls people to worship Him.

phrases.translation: He is inviting you in order to forgive your sins, and delay your end until your appointed term.”
phrases.explanation: Allah invites people to seek forgiveness and delays their end until an appointed time. The delay gives them an opportunity to repent rather than proving that judgment will never come.

phrases.translation: They argued, “You are no more than humans like us! You ˹only˺ wish to turn us away from what our forefathers worshipped. So bring us some compelling proof.”
phrases.explanation: The people answer that the messengers are only human and accuse them of turning people from ancestral worship. Their appeal to tradition substitutes inherited practice for evidence. They demand compelling proof. The request follows their rejection of the messengers’ explanation and sets up the answer that signs are under Allah’s authority.

phrases.translation: Their messengers said to them, “We are ˹indeed˺ only humans like you, but Allah favours whoever He chooses of His servants. It is not for us to bring you any proof without Allah’s permission. And in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: The messengers agree that they are human, but say Allah favors whichever servants He chooses. Being human does not prevent someone from carrying a message entrusted by Allah. The messengers cannot produce a sign on demand without Allah’s permission. They are conveyors of guidance, not independent sources of miracles. They tell believers to place their trust in Allah. Reliance on Him is especially important when opponents demand signs or threaten the messengers.

phrases.translation: Why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has truly guided us to ˹the very best of˺ ways?
phrases.explanation: The messengers ask why they should not trust Allah after He has guided them to the best ways. Guidance received becomes a reason for continued reliance, even when hardship follows.

phrases.translation: Indeed, we will patiently endure whatever harm you may cause us. And in Allah let the faithful put their trust.”
phrases.explanation: They promise to endure patiently whatever harm their opponents cause. Their trust does not mean they feel no danger, but that they will remain faithful under pressure. The faithful are again urged to trust Allah. The repetition reinforces reliance as a shared response for believers facing hostility.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers then threatened their messengers, “We will certainly expel you from our land, unless you return to our faith.” So their Lord revealed to them, “We will surely destroy the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers threaten to expel the messengers unless they return to the opponents’ faith. The ultimatum uses political power to pressure people to abandon their convictions. Allah reveals that the wrongdoers will be destroyed. The response places the final outcome in divine hands rather than allowing the threat of expulsion to decide the truth.

phrases.translation: and make you reside in the land after them. This is for whoever is in awe of standing before Me and fears My warning.”
phrases.explanation: Allah promises to let the messengers reside in the land after the wrongdoers are destroyed. The promise is tied to those who fear standing before Allah and take His warning seriously. The verse frames future security as a consequence of reverence and accountability. Power in the land is temporary, while the fear of Allah guides how people use it.

phrases.translation: And both sides called for judgment, so every stubborn tyrant was doomed
phrases.explanation: Both sides call for judgment, and every stubborn tyrant is doomed. The verse portrays the conflict as reaching a decision in which oppression does not escape its consequence. Their tyranny and arrogance meet a final judgment.

phrases.translation: Awaiting them is Hell, and they will be left to drink oozing pus
phrases.explanation: Hell awaits the tyrants, where they are left to drink oozing pus. The harsh image presents punishment as a real and degrading consequence of their persistent oppression. The image underscores the humiliation of their final state.

phrases.translation: which they will sip with difficulty, and can hardly swallow. Death will overwhelm them from every side, yet they will not ˹be able to˺ die. Awaiting them still is harsher torment
phrases.explanation: They sip the drink with difficulty and can barely swallow it. The description conveys the severity of their suffering rather than any relief from the punishment. Death overwhelms them from every direction, but they are not able to die. The verse portrays an existence from which neither escape nor relief is possible. Harsher torment still awaits them. The warning emphasizes that their suffering does not end with the first punishment described.

phrases.translation: The parable of the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that of ashes fiercely blown away by wind on a stormy day.
phrases.explanation: The deeds of those who disbelieve are compared to ashes scattered by fierce wind. The image shows how easily their efforts can be swept away when they are not grounded in faith.

phrases.translation: They will gain nothing from what they have earned. That is ˹truly˺ the farthest one can stray
phrases.explanation: They gain nothing from their deeds. What seemed valuable in worldly life cannot provide lasting benefit when it is detached from belief and right purpose. This is the farthest kind of straying. The parable concludes that rejecting Allah leaves a person without the lasting result they expected from their efforts.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth for a reason? If He wills, He can eliminate you and produce a new creation
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether people have seen that Allah created the heavens and earth for a reason. Creation is purposeful, not an accident without meaning or accountability. If Allah wills, He can remove people and create a new creation. The statement affirms that replacing one generation or creation is not difficult for Him.

phrases.translation: And that is not difficult for Allah ˹at all˺
phrases.explanation: Creating a new creation is not difficult for Allah. The statement closes the argument by contrasting divine power with human doubts about resurrection and replacement. No limit in creation can restrict His power.

phrases.translation: They will all appear before Allah, and the lowly ˹followers˺ will appeal to the arrogant ˹leaders˺, “We were your ˹dedicated˺ followers, so will you ˹then˺ protect us from Allah’s torment in any way?” They will reply, “Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you.
phrases.explanation: The lowly followers ask their arrogant leaders to protect them from Allah’s punishment. Their question shows that following powerful people cannot shield anyone from personal accountability. The leaders reply that they too would have guided their followers if Allah had guided them. Their answer shifts responsibility away from their own choices rather than offering help.

phrases.translation: ˹Now˺ it is all the same for us whether we suffer patiently or impatiently, there is no escape for us.”
phrases.explanation: Both groups face the same result whether they endure patiently or impatiently, because there is no escape. The verse shows that regret after judgment cannot undo the choices that led there.

phrases.translation: And Satan will say ˹to his followers˺ after the judgment has been passed, “Indeed, Allah has made you a true promise. I too made you a promise, but I failed you. I did not have any authority over you. I only called you, and you responded to me.
phrases.explanation: After judgment, Satan admits that Allah’s promise was true while his own promise failed. The admission exposes the false hope he offered to those who followed him. Satan says he had no authority over his followers and only called them, while they chose to respond. His words distinguish temptation from compulsion.

phrases.translation: So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot save you, nor can you save me. Indeed, I denounce your previous association of me with Allah ˹in loyalty˺. Surely the wrongdoers will suffer a painful punishment.”
phrases.explanation: He tells them not to blame him but themselves. The speech places responsibility on people who chose to follow a misleading invitation. Satan says he cannot save them and disowns their earlier association of him with Allah. The relationship they imagined offers no support at judgment. The wrongdoers will face painful punishment. Satan’s final words leave his followers without the rescue they expected from him.

phrases.translation: Those who believe and do good will be admitted into Gardens, under which rivers flow—to stay there forever by the Will of their Lord—where they will be greeted with “Peace!”
phrases.explanation: Believers who do good are admitted to Gardens with rivers beneath them, where they remain forever by Allah’s will. Their greeting is peace, expressing safety and welcome in their lasting home.

phrases.translation: Do you not see how Allah compares a good word to a good tree? Its root is firm and its branches reach the sky
phrases.explanation: Allah compares a good word to a good tree. The image presents sound belief or speech as something living that can grow and bear lasting benefit. The tree has firm roots and branches reaching the sky. Its stability and reach illustrate how truth can be grounded and still extend outward.

phrases.translation: ˹always˺ yielding its fruit in every season by the Will of its Lord. This is how Allah sets forth parables for the people, so perhaps they will be mindful
phrases.explanation: The good tree yields fruit in every season by its Lord’s will. Its continuing benefit depends on Allah, even when its roots and branches are strong. Allah gives parables so people may be mindful. The tree helps make the enduring value of a good word easier to understand and remember.

phrases.translation: And the parable of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from the earth, having no stability
phrases.explanation: An evil word is compared to a tree uprooted from the earth with no lasting stability. Unlike the good tree, it has no firm foundation and cannot produce lasting benefit.

phrases.translation: Allah makes the believers steadfast with the firm Word ˹of faith˺ in this worldly life and the Hereafter. And Allah leaves the wrongdoers to stray. For Allah does what He wills
phrases.explanation: Allah makes believers steadfast through the firm word of faith in this life and the Hereafter. Faith gives them stability during worldly trials and at final judgment. Allah leaves wrongdoers to stray. The contrast shows that people do not all respond to guidance in the same way. Allah does what He wills. His authority governs guidance and judgment, and no one can compel Him to follow human demands.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen those ˹disbelievers˺ who meet Allah’s favours with ingratitude and lead their own people to their doom
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether people have seen disbelievers answer Allah’s favors with ingratitude and lead their own people to ruin. Their influence harms others as well as themselves. Their ingratitude turns blessing into a source of harm.

phrases.translation: In Hell they will burn. What an evil place for settlement
phrases.explanation: Those who lead people toward ruin will burn in Hell, described as an evil place to settle. The verse names the consequence of ingratitude and misguidance. Its permanence makes the warning especially serious.

phrases.translation: They set up equals to Allah to mislead ˹others˺ from His Way. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Enjoy yourselves! Surely your destination is the Fire.”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers set up equals to Allah and use them to turn others away from His path. The verse condemns both associating partners with Allah and spreading that practice. The Prophet is told to say that they may enjoy themselves for now, but their destination is the Fire. Temporary pleasure does not cancel the final consequence.

phrases.translation: Tell My believing servants to establish prayer and donate from what We have provided for them—openly and secretly—before the arrival of a Day in which there will be no ransom or friendly connections
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to establish prayer and give from Allah’s provision, whether openly or privately. Worship and generosity are presented as practical responses to the gifts they receive. They should act before a Day when ransom and friendly connections will not help. The warning makes the time for prayer and charity the present life, before judgment arrives.

phrases.translation: It is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and sends down rain from the sky, causing fruits to grow as a provision for you. He has subjected the ships for your service, sailing through the sea by His command, and has subjected the rivers for you
phrases.explanation: Allah created the heavens and earth and sends rain that produces fruits for people. The verse links creation and rainfall with the food that sustains daily life. Ships sail through the sea by Allah’s command. Their usefulness depends on natural forces and human skill that remain within His created order. Allah has also subjected the rivers for people. These waterways provide resources and routes that support life and travel.

phrases.translation: He has ˹also˺ subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constantly orbiting, and has subjected the day and night for you
phrases.explanation: The sun and moon follow their courses, and Allah has also subjected day and night. Their regular cycles make time measurable and support the rhythms of human life. The verse presents these systems as favors placed at people’s service. Their order invites gratitude to Allah rather than pride in human control.

phrases.translation: And He has granted you all that you asked Him for. If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you would never be able to number them. Indeed humankind is truly unfair, ˹totally˺ ungrateful
phrases.explanation: Allah has granted people what they asked Him for. The verse describes provision as abundant, including gifts people may not always notice or name. People could never count all of Allah’s blessings, yet humanity is often unfair and ungrateful. The contrast calls for humility and a more attentive response to what has been given.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Abraham prayed, “My Lord! Make this city ˹of Mecca˺ secure, and keep me and my children away from the worship of idols
phrases.explanation: Abraham prays for Mecca to be secure and asks Allah to keep him and his children away from idol worship. His prayer recognizes that safety and faith both depend on Allah’s protection.

phrases.translation: My Lord! They have caused many people to go astray. So whoever follows me is with me, and whoever disobeys me—then surely You are ˹still˺ All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Abraham says idols have led many people astray. He asks Allah to protect his family from that influence and distinguishes his followers from those who disobey. Abraham says whoever follows him is with him. He identifies shared faith as the basis of this bond rather than ancestry alone. For those who disobey, Abraham asks Allah’s forgiveness and mercy. His prayer recognizes that Allah remains compassionate and can forgive those who turn back.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! I have settled some of my offspring in a barren valley, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of ˹believing˺ people incline towards them
phrases.explanation: Abraham has settled some of his descendants in a barren valley near Allah’s Sacred House so they can establish prayer. The place is difficult, but the purpose is worship. He asks Allah to make the hearts of believing people incline toward his family. Their support would help sustain a community in a remote place.

phrases.translation: and provide them with fruits, so perhaps they will be thankful
phrases.explanation: Abraham asks Allah to provide the family with fruits. The prayer seeks necessary provision where the valley itself is barren. He hopes that the family will be thankful. Abraham connects receiving provision with gratitude to the One who answers the prayer.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! You certainly know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah
phrases.explanation: Abraham affirms that Allah knows what people conceal and reveal, and that nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from Him. The statement grounds his prayer in complete divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: All praise is for Allah who has blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Lord is indeed the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers
phrases.explanation: Abraham praises Allah for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age. He recognizes the sons as blessings and calls Allah the Hearer of prayers. He sees the sons as blessings, not possessions.

phrases.translation: My Lord! Make me and those ˹believers˺ of my descendants keep up prayer. Our Lord! Accept my prayers
phrases.explanation: Abraham asks Allah to make him and believing descendants steadfast in prayer. His concern extends beyond himself to the worship of future generations. He asks Allah to accept his prayers. The request closes with humility, recognizing that worship itself depends on Allah’s acceptance.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the judgment will come to pass.”
phrases.explanation: Abraham asks Allah to forgive him, his parents, and the believers on the Day of Judgment. The prayer extends beyond his own fate to his family and the community of faith.

phrases.translation: Do not think ˹O Prophet˺ that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when ˹their˺ eyes will stare in horror—
phrases.explanation: Allah is not unaware of what wrongdoers do. He delays their punishment until a Day when their eyes stare in horror, so the delay should never be mistaken for ignorance or approval.

phrases.translation: rushing forth, heads raised, never blinking, hearts void
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers rush forward with raised heads, unable to blink and with empty hearts. The image portrays their terror and helplessness when judgment arrives. This dramatic imagery shows their speech and sight overwhelmed by fear.

phrases.translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will overtake ˹the wicked among˺ them, and the wrongdoers will cry, “Our Lord! Delay us for a little while. We will respond to Your call and follow the messengers!” ˹It will be said,˺ “Did you not swear before that you would never be removed ˹to the next life˺?”
phrases.explanation: The people are warned of a Day when punishment will overtake the wicked. The warning gives them an opportunity to respond before the consequence becomes immediate. When punishment arrives, the wrongdoers ask for more time so they can answer Allah’s call and follow the messengers. Their request comes too late, after rejecting the opportunity in life. They are reminded that they had sworn they would never be removed to the next life. The question exposes the contradiction between their earlier denial and their present plea.

phrases.translation: You passed by the ruins of those ˹destroyed peoples˺ who had wronged themselves. It was made clear to you how We dealt with them, and We gave you ˹many˺ examples
phrases.explanation: The audience has passed by the ruins of peoples who wronged themselves. Their remains are visible evidence that unjust communities do not remain secure forever. Allah’s treatment of those earlier peoples was made clear, and many examples were given. The history is meant to teach the audience rather than remain a distant report. The examples invite people to learn before facing a similar outcome. Remembering earlier communities can turn warning into an opportunity to change.

phrases.translation: They devised every plot, which was fully known to Allah, but their plotting was not enough to ˹even˺ overpower mountains ˹let alone Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers devise many plots, but every one is fully known to Allah. Secrecy from other people cannot hide their plans from the One who sees all. Their plotting cannot overpower mountains, much less Allah. The comparison exposes how small human schemes are beside the power of their Creator.

phrases.translation: So do not think ˹O Prophet˺ that Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers. Allah is indeed Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to think Allah will fail to keep His promise to the messengers. Allah is Almighty and capable of punishment, so the promised outcome is certain even if delayed.

phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the earth will be changed into a different earth and the heavens as well, and all will appear before Allah—the One, the Supreme
phrases.explanation: The earth and heavens will be changed, and all will appear before Allah, the One and Supreme. The verse presents the Day of Judgment as a complete transformation followed by universal accountability.

phrases.translation: On that Day you will see the wicked bound together in chains
phrases.explanation: On that Day, the wicked are seen bound together in chains. The image expresses their confinement and the loss of freedom that follows their wrongdoing. Their chains show that they cannot free themselves by collective strength.

phrases.translation: with garments of tar, and their faces covered with flames
phrases.explanation: The wicked wear garments of tar and their faces are covered with flames. The severe imagery conveys humiliation and punishment at the final judgment. No worldly clothing can shield them from the consequence.

phrases.translation: As such, Allah will reward every soul for what it has committed. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: Allah rewards every soul according to what it has done. The verse affirms individual accountability, so no person’s deeds are overlooked or assigned to someone else. Allah is swift in reckoning. His judgment does not require the limits of human time or leave any deed unresolved.

phrases.translation: This ˹Quran˺ is a ˹sufficient˺ message for humanity so that they may take it as a warning and know that there is only One God, and so that people of reason may be mindful
phrases.explanation: The Quran is presented as a sufficient message for all humanity. It gives people what they need to hear the warning and consider their relationship with Allah. The message warns people and calls them to know that there is only one God. The surah’s stories and arguments return to this central truth. People of reason are urged to be mindful. Reflection should lead to awareness of Allah and careful conduct in light of the final judgment.
